oil.summary: Crude pulled back modestly on the day — WTI off 0.32% to $81.87/bbl, Brent down 0.40% to $87.35 — but both benchmarks remain sharply higher on the week (+8% and +10% respectively), anchored by the ongoing Hormuz disruption. Iran's release of six tough conditions for reopening the strait dashed near-term peace hopes, while Bloomberg data confirmed transits remained largely disrupted as of Monday morning. OPEC output recovered 1.17 mb/d in July though still trails quota targets, and ADNOC issued its eighth spot tender since June as the UAE scrambles to redirect barrels westward. A sweeping US Russia-Iran sanctions bill advanced through the House after Senate passage, adding a further supply-risk premium. RBOB gasoline was the notable outlier, cratering 8.94% on the session — a move the provided data does not explain beyond broader crack-spread dynamics. Heating oil surged 10% on the week, consistent with the worsening global diesel crunch flagged in headlines.
drivers: Strait of Hormuz remains heavily disrupted; Iran's tough reopening conditions kill near-term ceasefire optimism, keeping a geopolitical premium in crude
US Congress advances sweeping Russia-Iran sanctions package, threatening additional supply constraints on both Russian and Iranian barrels
RBOB gasoline collapsed 8.94% intraday — a sharp outlier relative to flat crude — while heating oil +10% on the week reflects deepening diesel-supply tightness ahead of winter
sources: ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos

gas.summary: Henry Hub was nearly flat on the day at $2.785/MMBtu (-0.32%), nudging higher on the week (+3.84%) but still down on the month (-3.87%), reflecting a market that remains structurally long supply even as geopolitical risk elsewhere rises. TTF fell sharply, -3.36% to €58.755/MWh, though the European benchmark is still up over 14% on the month, signalling residual Hormuz-driven LNG supply anxiety easing slightly today. The dominant theme in headlines is gas-as-growth: JP Morgan data show global gas turbine orders hit a record high in Q2 as power demand surges, and the US offshore wind retreat — framed as a $4 billion retrenchment — is being read as a structural bet on cheap gas persisting. Colombia's reversal of its four-year renewable push back toward oil and gas exploration adds another demand-side signal.
drivers: Record global gas turbine orders (per JP Morgan Q2 data) signal accelerating structural shift toward gas-fired power generation
US offshore-wind cancellations worth $4 billion reinforce the market narrative of durable, low-cost US gas underpinning generation economics
TTF -3.36% on the day suggests modest easing of European LNG supply anxiety, though the contract is still +14.6% on the month reflecting Hormuz-driven carry

power.summary: EU carbon EUAs ticked up 1.35% to $78.96/EUA, extending a quiet but steady grind higher (+3.1% on the month), even as TTF dropped 3.36% on the session. The carbon-gas spread move is noteworthy: softer gas prices reduce the marginal cost of power generation, which can dampen near-term EUA demand, yet prices still firmed — suggesting underlying confidence in the emissions cap trajectory. The key narrative crosscurrents for the power sector today are: record gas turbine orders pointing to higher future fossil-fuel burn intensity, the US offshore-wind retreat signalling slower clean-capacity build-out, and ongoing Iran-war uncertainty keeping LNG and pipeline supply risk elevated. Headline flow on the Hormuz situation dominates the macro backdrop for European power costs, though no specific power-price data beyond EUAs and TTF were provided.
drivers: EUAs +1.35% despite softer TTF, suggesting carbon market participants are pricing medium-term supply tightness rather than reacting to today's gas move
Record gas turbine orders and US wind-project cancellations point to higher fossil-fuel intensity in the global power mix, structurally supportive for carbon demand
Iran war exit conditions remain unresolved; Hormuz disruption continues to underpin LNG supply-risk premium embedded in European power costs via TTF
